links.note: The answer opens 'whether a credit would be useful or not will depend on risks involved, whether there is some support against a loss, terms of credit' - 23794's description exactly. 23793 is the debt trap that results when the risk materialises; this stem asks what determines the outcome.
How money solves the double coincidence of wants, by acting as an intermediate step in exchange - 23784's description.
What banks do with deposits: keep about 15 per cent as cash and lend the major portion. 23789 word for word. 23790 is the interest spread that follows, which this stem does not ask.

The inscription on a ten-rupee note - Reserve Bank of India, guaranteed by the Central Government, the Governor's promise to pay. That is 23786, currency issued by the RBI on behalf of the central government. 23785 is why people accept it, not who issues it.
Why formal credit must be expanded, argued from informal lenders charging 3-5 per cent a month and imposing tough side-conditions. The stem is about the formal sector, 23798.

The basic idea behind SHGs - organising the rural poor, especially women, to pool savings and borrow without collateral. 23801. 23802 is the narrower point that group membership substitutes for collateral.
Why banks refuse some borrowers; the answer's decisive reason is the absence of collateral. 23796. 23795 is the full set of credit terms, of which this item isolates one.

RBI supervision of banks - monitoring cash balances, requiring lending to small cultivators and small borrowers, collecting information on loans. 23798's description names RBI supervision as what marks the formal sector.

Credit's role in development: loans to industry and trade raising production, employment and profits. That is 23792, credit that leaves the borrower better off. The answer's caution about high risk reaches 23794.
Manav choosing between a bank and a moneylender on interest, repayment terms and collateral, with the answer noting formal-sector terms are generally better - 23797, terms differing between lenders.

Four parts about small farmers: why banks refuse them, what other sources exist, how terms can be unfavourable, and how they might get cheap credit. The unifying concept is 23797 - terms varying by lender with the poor facing the harshest. Individual parts reach 23796, 23799 and 23800.

Five blanks; the first and governing one is that the majority of POOR households' credit needs are met from informal sources, which is 23799's finding. The others touch 23793, 23786, 23790 and 23796 one each.
Decisions on savings and loans in an SHG being taken by the members is 23801's description of how a self-help group works.

The definition of credit - the lender supplying money, goods or services against a promise of future payment. No concept in this frame holds that bare definition; 23791 is the nearest, being the loan agreement and its repayment. 23795 covers the terms attached to a loan rather than what a loan is.
A typical SHG having 15-20 members is a fact about the group's composition, 23801.
Collateral as an asset of the borrower used as a guarantee to the lender - 23796's description verbatim.

Paper notes as the modern form of currency, against gold, silver and copper. The point is that modern currency has no use of its own and is accepted because the government authorises it - 23785. 23786 names paper notes but is about who issues them.
Moneylenders charging much higher interest than banks is 23799's description of informal lending.
Nobody supervising informal-sector lenders is 23799's 'no supervision' clause; 23798 is the supervised formal counterpart, which the distractors point at.

Plastic money as the form increasingly used alongside paper money - a cashless instruction to the bank to pay from the account, which is the mechanism 23788 describes for cheques. 23787 is the deposit itself rather than the means of paying from it.
Exchanging goods for goods as the barter system - the problem money solves, which 23784 states.
All three keyed functions (removing double coincidence of wants, common measure of value, standard of deferred payment) belong to money as the medium of exchange, 23784.
